newsitem.title: POLAND: South Africa's Stals hints at H2 monetary relaxing.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Stals hints at H2 monetary relaxing.

text.p: The South African Reserve Bank may relax its monetary policy in the second half of this year if there is a slowdown in inflation, the growth of money supply and credit extension, Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday.

"Inflation..is now about nine percent and we would like to see the rate of inflation come down to a lower level before we will relax the monetary policy," Stals told a news conference after meeting his Polish counterpart in Warsaw.

"It is not impossible that this (relaxing of monetary policy) will be in the second half of this year, but this is just speculation and the central bank would like to see the statistics before we will move," he added.

Stals said money supply was growing at year-on-year 14 to 15 percent, higher than the 10 percent growth written into guidelines, while credit extension was increasing at about 17 percent, above the desired 12 to 13 percent growth.

Earlier on Wedneday Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said in Japan that South Afica's interest rates may be lowered later this year. "Indications are positieve for some reduction in interest rates later this year," he said.
